overview: This file documents the disappearance and discovery of a Japan Air Transport Company passenger aircraft, the Envoy (DAOL), during a flight from Giran to Taihoku in northern Taiwan on March 7, 1940. American Consul Gerald Warner first reported the missing aircraft, its eight occupants—including German mechanical engineer Enno Topp—and the weather-hampered search, while emphasizing that no Americans were aboard. A subsequent despatch reported that the wreckage had been found on Qixing Mountain and that everyone aboard had died; the papers also discuss previous regional air accidents and proposed improvements to radio, weather-reporting, telephone, and routing arrangements. The bundle includes the initial despatch, a confirmation copy of Warner’s telegram to Tokyo, the follow-up despatch, and a map enclosure locating the crash.

subfiles.title: Despatch No. 97 on the disappearance of the Envoy
subfiles.about: Reports the disappearance of a Japan Air Transport Company passenger aircraft between Giran and Taihoku and confirms that no Americans were aboard.
subfiles.summary: Warner reports the Envoy disappeared with eight aboard, no radio, prompting a 6,000-person search and proposals for radios and better weather reporting.

subfiles.title: Confirmation copy of Warner’s telegram to Tokyo
subfiles.about: Briefly alerts the Tokyo consulate to the missing aircraft, its passengers, the unsuccessful search, and the absence of American casualties.
subfiles.summary: Telegram confirms the Envoy disappeared with eight aboard including a German engineer, no Americans involved, fog hampering search.

subfiles.title: Despatch reporting discovery of the Envoy wreckage
subfiles.about: Reports that the missing Envoy had been found wrecked on Qixing Mountain and that all eight occupants were killed.
subfiles.summary: Warner reports the Envoy's wreckage found demolished near Qixing Mountain, all eight killed instantly; Taiwan's government handled the German victim's remains.

subfiles.title: Map showing the site of the Envoy crash
subfiles.about: Locates the March 7, 1940 crash of the Envoy on the side of Qixing Mountain.
subfiles.summary: Map encloses the Envoy crash site, noting all eight aboard died, mountain name possibly OCR-corrupted.

interest: Shows a missing-aircraft search and crash-site discovery in Taiwan, with details on navigation and emergency response.
